title: Expected linear time for the relative neighborhood graph of uniform points in the unit cube
abstract: A Lean 4 proof about an algorithm (SPoIF, Secure Posts on Increasing Fence) that computes the relative neighborhood graph of N points of the unit cube in three dimensions. The points are binned into a grid of about N cells. For each point p, a cube of grid cells around p (the fence) grows until the points collected inside it cut every patch of its surface off from p: a patch is cut off by a collected point q when it lies beyond the plane through q with normal q - p, so that q lies in the lune of p and any point beyond the patch. The neighbours of p are then found among the collected points by the direct lune test. Two theorems are proved. Correctness: for any points of the cube, the neighbours reported at each point are exactly its neighbours in the relative neighborhood graph. Expected linear time: for N independent uniform points of the cube, the expected operation count of the whole algorithm is at most C N for a constant C.
